x: With Steve White and Arnold Bent having collected four golds and a silver between them our supporters were really cock-a-hoop, for young L.J.
Lee Sullivan was our next point of interest and, although he had clocked a 10.3 seconds 100 yards at an earlier schools meeting, he opted for the Intermediate Boys (under 17) long jump.
On 20th July two Bels., Lee Sullivan and Bill Curtin, travelled up to Solihull, Birmingham to represent London in the All England Boys Club Championships.

In the international match at Crystal Palace, Bill (4:07) placed 2nd to the German boy (4:05) who must have had to go some to beat Bill on this track. Also now sporting a German vest (exchanged at this meeting) is Lee Sullivan who represented London in the long jump.
Lee Sullivan 19' 9" 1500 metres youths John Stow 4:41.0 Ed McNally 4:49.0

Steve White, Bill Curtin, Martin Bloice, Richard Langley, Arnold Bentt, Lee Sullivan and Peter Carton are just a few of the names that come to mind and (dare we hope?) seem to have overcome the difficult periods which face all youngsters who try to take their athletics seriously.

Lee Sullivan just missed the final with 11.5. Both these athletes also played their part in the finest "clean-sweep" of the Championships when, with Arnold Bent making up the trio, they all cleared over 21'-0" in the Junior Long Jump with the medal order reading White, Sullivan, Bentt.

Title holders Steve White (21.7) and Lee Sullivan (21'-9½") had no difficulty in holding on to their number one positions in the Senior ranks, but Arnold Bent relinquished his high jump title to rival Alexander who won on the count back---both clearing 5'-9¾".

Lee Sullivan added six inches to his previous best in taking third place in the long jump with 22'-5¾". A below par Bill Curtin was drawn in the same heat of the 1500 metres as John Stowe but neither made the final---Bill being 4th (4:09.4) and John 5th (4:11.2).
Lee Sullivan represented the London Boroughs versus Israel, France and Germany on July 24th in Germany, winning the long jump with 22'-2¼" and finishing second in the 100 metres with 11.3
Lee Sullivan shared the same time (11.5) as the first and second when being placed third in the Junior 100 metres in a S.C.A.A.A. open meeting at Crystal Palace on Oct 15th.

Lee Sullivan was a split second and ¾" away from real success. He just failed to make the final of the 100 metres and then with an excellent jump of 22'-7¾" had to give best by ¾" to Rose (QPH) in the long jump.

Other winners were Lee Sullivan (Junior long jump), our Senior sprint relay team and Colin Gillett (400 hurdles) who also featured prominently in the flat 400.

Heaviest loaded with trophies and medals were Lee Sullivan (Jun), who notched the senior long jump title in addition to the Junior's sprint double, and John Cambridge (Boy) who scooped an unusual trio in the Boys 100, 800 and high jump.
4 x 100 metres · 4. Belgrave (L. Sullivan,M. Marshall,D. McMillan,S. White) · 46.0

Our winners were Bruno Hafner ('B' 100 metres), Lionel Mann ('B' 5000 metres), Alan Black ('B' steeplechase), Charlie Gillett ('B' 400 metres hurdles), Arnold Bentt ('A' High Jump), Bob Couillault ('B' Triple Jump) and the 4 x 100 metres relay team of Lee Sullivan, Bruno Hafner, Charlie Gillett and Steve White.
Peter Carton has the distinction of filling 11th place in the 800m., and 18th in the 5,000m., while John Stow shows up in 17th place over 3,000m. In the long-jump, Lee Sullivan is 13th.
He will have fine backing from LEE SULLIVAN, MICK MARSHALL, CLIFF BROOKS and CHARLIE GILLETT. 400m One of the weak spots, although I hope I'am proved wrong.
Lee Sullivan also had a good start to the season in the Long Jump winning with 21' 7" and showing fine consistancy by clearing this exact distance on three of his attempts.

These included some good sprinting from Cliff Brooks and Lee Sullivan, and some good long-jumping from the same pair. But pride of place undoubtedly went to the shot-putt, where Cliff shoved the benefit of technique training with a distance of 41' 4½", and John Martin was also over 40'.
Lee Sullivan was probably our outstanding senior competitor, but came up against some exceptionally hot competition in the 100m. and long-jump.
Mick Marshall, Philip Gee, Chris Martin and Lee Sullivan were third in the sprint relay, and it was particularly good to see Chris sporting a Belgrave vest again.
Lee Sullivan is just out of them, and another up and coming athlete. In the "B" long-jump, he was edged into second place by just 1½".

On the same evening the 300m handicap saw a fine run by the scratch man Lee Sullivan to get a first place. Getting to the end of May now and at the Inter-Counties Championships at Leicester on Monday, 29th May John Bicourt finished second in the 3,000m steeplechase with 8m 46s.
